reason: The cited evidence shows that annealing of a supersaturated BCC solid solution leads to segregation and subsequent formation of σ and B2 phases (E3), and that internal stresses arise from σ-phase formation (E1), but none of the passages directly demonstrates that elastic strains from segregation are the trigger for nucleation, nor do they quantify a strain threshold or link cooling-rate-dependent segregation to strain-driven transformation in the specific Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 alloy.
premises: Differential elemental diffusion during cooling creates localized segregation
Segregation produces elastic lattice strains due to atomic size misfit
Elastic strains exceeding a threshold trigger nucleation of secondary phases
Secondary phases (σ, B2) relieve elastic energy and lower free energy
Cooling rate controls segregation extent and thus phase transformation
